**Finding submitted: deviation (fallback-level cure).**

- **Responsive clause:** Section 1.4 (p0008–p0009) is the only inbound grant to us — access to and the right to use HDI's hosting system, software and Content administration tools. The only other licence (p0038–p0039, Deerskin Marks) runs *from* us to HDI, so it is outside this rule.
- **Gap:** the grant runs to "the Company" only, and "Company" is defined as The Deerskin Companies, Inc. with no affiliate concept anywhere in the document (no "Affiliate" hits), so the fallback affiliate element fails.
- **Already met:** the successor element is satisfied verbatim by Section 10.3 (p0063), under which the Agreement inures to the benefit of and is enforceable by the parties' successors and assigns — no duplicate successor language added.
- **Not walk-away:** the grant is not expressly revocable at HDI's discretion.
- **Cure:** one short inserted sentence extending the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates on written notice, leaving all existing wording verbatim. Preferred extras (contractors, perpetual/irrevocable) noted in the rationale but not volunteered at the fallback target.
